chose: 3.5 peer hint, built as: the lease hook appends {task, session} to its lane's lease whenever its host session changes (latest wins); checkLease returns the older holders a FRESH steer/refusal or a hook notice named whose lease carries a session; lease-hook.ts resolves them and its own session through core/peers.ts and, only when both are live in Claude Code's registry, adds one line (packets.ts peerHint, ≤400 chars) naming each holder by its SendMessage name. No hint on a repeat collision, the launch notice, or any session absent from the registry (Codex, Cursor, cloud, ended).
over: The session id in the lease header (the coordinator writes it before the session exists, and a relaunch changes it). A hint in the launch notice (no collision yet, tokens on lanes it may never touch). Gating on the hook adapter alone (the registry check names Codex/Cursor/cloud on both sides without knowing the adapter). sofar posting to the peer socket (peers.ts: addressing layer only).
because: A holder can only collide once its hook has claimed, so the hook that claims already knows the session to name. Gating on a fresh collision keeps the hint to roughly 60 tokens, once per holder. Checking the registry on both sides means a session that cannot SendMessage, or a holder nobody can reach, gets exactly the 3.3 packet it got before.
